prompt:
You are a careful equity research analyst. Assess the competitive advantages (economic moat) and pricing power of the publicly listed company "SHOPIFY INC." (ticker SHOP), and list its competitors. Use the most recent information you know. Never invent figures: use null when unsure. Be specific (products, numbers, years).

Reply with ONLY one JSON object, no other text, in exactly this shape:
{
 "name": "official company name", "ticker": "SHOP", "industry": "industry in a few words",
 "markets": ["the main product markets it competes in"],
 "mission": {"statement": "the company's own official mission statement, word for word as it publishes it; null if you are not sure of the exact wording (never paraphrase here)",
             "source": "where it is published, e.g. company website or 2025 annual report, or null",
             "plain": "what the mission means, in one short simple sentence"},
 "about": {"plain": "3-4 short sentences explaining what the company does, in simple everyday words a 12-year-old would understand; no jargon",
           "customers": "who buys from it, in one simple sentence",
           "everyday": "one sentence linking it to something ordinary people know or use, or null",
           "money": [ {"part": "business line in simple words", "share": decimal share of sales or null, "plain": "what it sells there, in a few simple words", "tag": "main|new|moonshot"} ]  (its main ways of making money, largest first, up to 6; also include any new business line or one with explosive, moonshot potential even if its sales are still small. tag: "main" = an established line that brings in a large part of sales; "new" = launched or entered in roughly the last 3 years; "moonshot" = could grow many times over or reshape the company, e.g. a new technology or market, even if unproven. Give each line one tag, the one that fits best)},
 "summary": "2-3 plain-English sentences on whether and why it has a competitive advantage",
 "pricingPower": {"rating": "strong|moderate|weak", "evidence": "specific evidence, e.g. price rises and what happened to volumes"},
 "moats": [ {"source": one of ["Brand and intangible assets","Switching costs","Network effects","Cost advantage and scale","Efficient scale","Counter-positioning","Process power (hard-to-copy know-how)","Cornered resource (exclusive asset or talent)"], "strength": "strong|moderate|weak|none", "evidence": "one or two specific sentences"} ]  (all 8 sources, in that order),
 "customers": {"rating": "strong|moderate|weak", "evidence": "customer satisfaction and loyalty: retention, NPS, reviews, repeat purchase"},
 "talent": {"rating": "strong|moderate|weak", "evidence": "ability to attract and keep top talent: employer rankings, reputation, pay"},
 "product": {"rating": "strong|moderate|weak", "evidence": "is the product best in class? independent benchmarks, awards, ecosystem"},
 "competitors": [ {"name": "company name", "ticker": "main listing ticker (exchange suffix if not US, e.g. 005930.KS) or null if private",
                   "usTicker": "ticker of its US listing or ADR that files reports with the SEC, or null", "overlap": "high|medium|low",
                   "note": "where they compete"} ]  (every significant competitor, most direct first, up to 15; include major private ones with ticker null),
 "estimates": [ {"name": "company name", "fy": "FY2025", "currency": "USD", "revenueUSDm": number, "revenueGrowth3y": decimal, "grossMargin": decimal, "operatingMargin": decimal, "netMargin": decimal} ]
   (approximate latest fiscal-year figures for the company itself and for every listed competitor; decimals, e.g. 0.42; null if unknown),
 "marketShare": [ {"market": "market name", "measure": "revenue|units|shipments|...", "latestYear": "2025", "earlierYear": "2020",
                   "rows": [ {"name": "company name", "latest": decimal or null, "earlier": decimal or null} ] } ]  (up to 3 of its main markets, the company and its main rivals),
 "threats": ["specific things that could weaken its advantage"],
 "ceo": {"name": "current CEO", "founder": true or false, "since": "YYYY", "background": "e.g. electrical engineer, Stanford MBA"},
 "checklist": { "<id>": {"verdict": "yes|partly|no|unknown", "evidence": "one specific sentence with names, numbers or examples"} }  for EVERY id below:
   "c1": Rule Breaker #1: is it the leader of an important industry that is still emerging and growing fast?
   "c2": Rule Breaker #2: why do customers choose it over rivals (brand, better value, innovation, culture, leadership), and is that advantage hard to copy and likely to last many years?
   "c3": Rule Breaker #5: do ordinary people recognise the name, is it the default leader in its field (like Google, Amazon, NVIDIA, Tesla, Intuitive Surgical, Netflix), and would customers recommend its product?
   "c4": Does it have an inspiring mission it keeps emphasising, with management driven by purpose rather than money? If it spends 10 years doing this, would it matter?
   "c6": What is the general public consensus about the company and its products or services? When people hear the name, what are the first few descriptive words that come to mind? Start the evidence with those words in quotes (e.g. “innovative, premium, reliable”), then say whether that impression is mostly positive.
   "c7": Is its total addressable market large and growing, riding a secular trend (like CRWD, NVDA, TSLA, AMZN)?
   "c8": Does it have room to expand into big new markets: in its name, its technology or its vision?
   "m1": Is the CEO a visionary with a clear picture of the future?
   "m2": Is the CEO a founder (or acting like one): long-term thinking, working extraordinarily hard, pouring heart and soul into building something that outlives them?
   "m4": Does the CEO lead by serving employees and customers?
   "m5": Has the CEO deliberately built a strong, distinctive culture that keeps inventing new products and technologies?
   "m6": Is the CEO deeply hands-on with the product and technology, ideally with an engineering background?
   "m7": Is the CEO a person of great character who cares about something bigger than profit? For successor CEOs: is stewardship aimed at the benefit of humanity?
   "m7b": Has the CEO been invited to give a commencement speech at a top university (Stanford, Harvard, MIT, etc.)? Name it.
   "m8b": Does the CEO have a distinctive, memorable personality (like Elon Musk, Alex Karp, Larry Page)?
   "m9": Has the CEO a strong record of execution and results?
   "m10": Is the CEO and company known for frugality (like Bezos's door desk)?
   "c10": Do its products solve problems for people all over the world, greatly improving the lives of a very large number of people (like NFLX, GOOG, ISRG)?
   "p2": Is what it builds extremely hard to do, and important to the world?
   "f1": Has revenue grown in almost every one of the last five years?
   "f2": Have gross and operating margins risen over the last five years?
   "f3": Is debt low compared with cash and cash flow, with positive shareholders' equity?
   "f4": Have operating income and operating cash flow risen over the last five years?
   "v1": Is its main product clearly the best in its field, with a practical reason an ordinary person can understand for choosing it over every alternative (like NVIDIA over AMD)?
   "v2": Is it widely seen as one of the best companies to work for (culture, mission, reputation, employer rankings)? Cite rankings.
   "c5": Do its products make the world better? If it disappeared overnight, who would notice and miss it, and why?
 "asOf": "YYYY-MM of the newest information you used"
}

result.name: Shopify Inc.
markets: E-commerce website and store software for merchants
Merchant payments and checkout (Shopify Payments, Shop Pay)
Merchant lending (Shopify Capital), shipping, tax and other merchant services
Selling through AI assistants and marketplaces (agentic commerce)

mission.statement: Our mission is to make commerce better for everyone.
mission.plain: It wants to make it easier for anyone to start and run a business that sells things.

about.plain: Shopify gives people the tools to build an online shop without needing to write code. It also takes the payments, helps with shipping, and offers card machines for real-world shops. Small sellers and huge brands both use it, and it earns a monthly fee plus a small cut of many sales. Shoppers often buy from Shopify stores without knowing it.
about.customers: Millions of businesses, from one-person startups to large brands, in more than 175 countries.
about.everyday: When you buy from a brand's own website and pay with the purple Shop Pay button, that store is usually running on Shopify.

money.plain: payment processing, Shop Pay, loans, shipping and other paid tools
monthly plans for online stores, apps and themes
card readers and software for real-world stores
store software for big brands and business buyers
letting shoppers buy Shopify products inside apps like ChatGPT

result.summary: Shopify has a real competitive advantage: merchants build their whole business on its platform and app ecosystem, so switching is painful, and its scale in checkout (Shop Pay) and payments keeps improving the offer. Revenue grew 30% to $11,556M in 2025 and 34% in Q2 2026, showing it keeps taking share, though Amazon, WooCommerce and others remain strong alternatives.

pricingPower.evidence: Shopify has raised subscription prices (for example its 2023 plan increases) and monthly recurring revenue still rose from $178M at end-2024 to $221M in Q2 2026, but much revenue is payment fees where it competes on price with Stripe, PayPal and others, and gross margin slipped from 53.8% in 2021 to 48.1% in 2025.

moats.evidence: Shopify is the best-known brand for building an online store, and Shop Pay is a trusted checkout button for shoppers, but most consumers do not know the stores they buy from use it.
Merchants run their catalogue, payments, apps, customer data, POS and lending on Shopify, so moving to another platform means rebuilding the store and retraining staff.
Thousands of app developers, theme designers and agency partners build for its large merchant base, and Shop Pay gets more useful to shoppers as more stores accept it.
With $378.4B of GMV in 2025 it can negotiate payment costs and spread R&D across millions of merchants, though Amazon is far larger.
E-commerce software is a large, open market with many rivals rather than one that supports only a few players.
Its model of 'arming the rebels' (helping brands own their customers) is hard for Amazon to copy without undermining its own marketplace.
Years of running checkout at huge scale (including Black Friday peaks) give it a high-converting, reliable checkout that is hard to match quickly.
It has no exclusive asset, though founder-CEO Tobi Lütke's long-term leadership is distinctive.

customers.evidence: Merchants stay and grow with it: MRR rose 24% from $178M (end-2024) to $221M (Q2 2026) while GMV grew 31.6% in Q2 2026, and large brands such as Mattel and Gymshark run on Shopify; no NPS figure is published.

talent.evidence: Shopify attracts strong engineers with a product-first, remote culture, but it cut about 20% of staff in 2023 and its 2025 'reflexive AI usage' memo and intense culture make it divisive rather than a top-ranked workplace.

product.evidence: Shopify is widely rated the leading e-commerce platform for independent brands, with a large App Store, Shop Pay checkout and fast product releases (twice-yearly 'Editions').

competitors.name: Amazon.com, Inc.
competitors.note: Marketplace that competes for merchants and shoppers; also Buy with Prime and Amazon Pay

competitors.name: WooCommerce (Automattic)
competitors.note: Free open-source e-commerce plug-in for WordPress websites

competitors.name: Commerce.com (formerly BigCommerce Holdings)
competitors.note: Hosted e-commerce software for mid-size and enterprise merchants

competitors.name: Wix.com Ltd.
competitors.note: Website builder with online store features for small businesses

competitors.name: Squarespace (owned by Permira)
competitors.note: Website builder with commerce tools for small sellers

competitors.name: Salesforce, Inc. (Commerce Cloud)
competitors.note: Enterprise e-commerce software for large brands

competitors.name: Block, Inc. (Square)
competitors.note: Point-of-sale, payments and online stores (Square Online) for small businesses

competitors.name: Lightspeed Commerce Inc.
competitors.note: Point-of-sale and e-commerce for retailers and restaurants, plus Ecwid

competitors.name: Stripe
competitors.note: Online payments and checkout for merchants

competitors.name: PayPal Holdings, Inc.
competitors.note: Online checkout and payments, competing with Shop Pay and Shopify Payments

competitors.name: MercadoLibre, Inc.
competitors.note: Marketplace and payments in Latin America

threats: Amazon using Buy with Prime and its marketplace to pull brands and shoppers away
AI shopping assistants (ChatGPT, Google, Perplexity) taking control of product discovery and checkout away from merchant stores
Payment competition from Stripe, PayPal and Apple Pay squeezing Shopify Payments fees
Tariffs and the end of the US de minimis exemption hurting small cross-border merchants
Lower-cost website builders and open-source WooCommerce at the small end, and Salesforce and Adobe at the enterprise end
High valuation that leaves little room for growth to slow

ceo.name: Tobias (Tobi) Lütke
ceo.background: Self-taught programmer from Germany who trained through a computer programming apprenticeship; co-founded Snowdevil, the snowboard shop that became Shopify, in 2004-2006

c1.evidence: Shopify leads independent e-commerce software in a still-growing industry, with GMV up from $292.3B in 2024 to $378.4B in 2025 and revenue up 34% in Q2 2026.

c2.evidence: Merchants choose it for ease of use, its App Store and Shop Pay checkout, and an all-in-one platform from online to POS to lending, an ecosystem that is hard to copy and deepens every year.

c3.evidence: Sellers and entrepreneurs know Shopify as the default platform and recommend it, but many ordinary shoppers do not recognise the name behind the stores they use.

c4.evidence: Its mission to 'make commerce better for everyone' runs through Lütke's letters and its 'arm the rebels' stance, and ten more years of lowering the cost of starting a business would matter to millions of entrepreneurs.

c6.evidence: “easy, online store, entrepreneurial”: the impression among sellers and investors is mostly positive, as the tool that lets anyone start a business.

c7.evidence: Global commerce keeps shifting online and into AI-driven channels, and Shopify's GMV of $378.4B in 2025 is still a small fraction of world retail.

c8.evidence: It is expanding into enterprise, B2B, offline retail POS, international markets and agentic commerce, including checkout inside ChatGPT announced in 2025.

m1.evidence: Tobi Lütke has a clear long-term picture of entrepreneurship and commerce, from 'arming the rebels' against Amazon to his 2025 push to make AI central to every role.

m2.evidence: Lütke founded the company and has run it since 2008, holds founder voting control through a founder share, and is known for long-term thinking.

m4.evidence: He is merchant-obsessed, but cutting about 20% of staff in 2023 and demanding AI-first work show a hard-driving rather than servant style toward employees.

m5.evidence: He built a distinctive builder culture (twice-yearly Editions releases, the 2023 meeting purge, the 2025 'reflexive AI usage' memo) that keeps shipping new products.

m6.evidence: Lütke is a programmer who wrote much of the original Shopify code and remains deeply involved in product and engineering.

m7.evidence: He focuses on empowering small entrepreneurs, but there is little public record of causes beyond the business.

m7b.evidence: No commencement speech by Tobi Lütke at a top university has been found.

m8b.evidence: Lütke is a memorable, outspoken figure known for blunt posts, his AI memo and his love of programming and gaming.

m9.evidence: Under Lütke revenue grew from $4,612M in 2021 to $11,556M in 2025, operating income reached $1,468M and free cash flow $2,007M in 2025.

m10.evidence: Shopify cut costs sharply after 2022 (selling its logistics arm to Flexport and cutting staff) and asks teams to prove AI cannot do a job before hiring, but it is not famous for frugal symbols.

c10.evidence: Millions of businesses in more than 175 countries use it to earn a living, and many millions of shoppers buy through its stores.

p2.evidence: Running checkout, payments and storefronts reliably at peak loads such as Black Friday is hard and important to entrepreneurs, though rivals offer similar tools.

f2.evidence: Operating margin rose from 5.8% in 2021 to 12.7% in 2025, but gross margin fell from 53.8% to 48.1% as lower-margin payments grew.

f3.evidence: After $1,043M of convertible notes matured in 2025 it held $4,947M of cash and marketable securities at June 30, 2026 against no reported borrowings, with $12,684M of equity.

f4.evidence: Operating income rose from $269M in 2021 to $1,468M in 2025 and free cash flow from $1,597M (2024) to $2,007M (2025), but there were operating losses of $822M in 2022 and $1,418M in 2023.

v1.evidence: For an independent brand it is usually the best choice because it is easy to set up and has the biggest app ecosystem, but Amazon's marketplace and cheaper builders such as Wix suit some sellers better.

v2.evidence: Shopify is admired by many engineers for its builder culture, but layoffs in 2023 and an intense AI-first culture mean it is not consistently named among the best places to work.

c5.evidence: If it disappeared, millions of small businesses and brands would lose their online stores and checkout overnight, and their customers would notice.
